name: Townhouse Interior
description: The whole map is the inside of one city building: hall, rooms and stairs behind a single outer wall.
palette: limewashed plaster, dark oak framing, honey floorboards, soot black, brass warmth
lighting: grey window light falling in from the outer walls, firelight from the hearths, lamps in the inner rooms
aesthetics: Hand-painted fantasy cartography, rough painterly brushwork with visible strokes, strong dark ink outlines around every object and wall, subtle black and brown linework, restrained desaturated colour, carefully shaded volumetric detail, inked line art over watercolour and gouache, premium hand-drawn D&D virtual tabletop map, dense environmental storytelling
ground: wide honey-coloured oak floorboards running the length of each room, worn pale along the walking lines, with woven rugs laid across them
materials: The inside of one substantial city townhouse seen from directly above with the roof taken off, filling the whole picture: a single building, not a street and not several houses. Thick limewashed plaster outer walls with dark oak framing enclose everything; lighter plastered partition walls divide the inside into rooms, and every doorway between them stands in one of those partitions. Wide oak floorboards run room by room, worn pale where people walk and covered here and there by woven rugs. The rooms are furnished and lived in: a long trestle table with benches, a stone hearth with a fire laid and a copper pot beside it, a curtained bed, a writing desk under a shuttered window, shelves of crockery and ledgers, a locked chest, storage barrels and crates stacked against an inner wall, a wooden staircase with its treads visible from above, and iron lamp brackets on the walls.
